title: Digging Patch & Allotment
strapline: A patch of real earth to dig, plant and harvest — the whole cycle of growing food, from seed to snack.
intent: Children experience the full arc of growing — digging, sowing, watering, waiting, harvesting and eating what they grew.
Children build patience and delayed gratification, learning that growing takes time and care over weeks and seasons.
Children develop strength and coordination through real physical work — digging, raking, hauling, watering.
Children understand where food comes from and take pride in eating vegetables they grew themselves.
Children observe change, life cycles and the seasons through plants they tend day after day.
implementation: Give over a real patch of earth or raised beds with proper child-sized tools — spades, forks, trowels, watering cans, a wheelbarrow.
Choose fast, forgiving, edible crops for early success — radishes, salad leaves, peas, potatoes, beans, sunflowers.
Let children do the real work, including the digging-for-its-own-sake — a patch just to dig and find worms is valuable too.
Share the tending as an ongoing responsibility — a watering rota, checking on shoots, pulling weeds — so children see the commitment growing takes.
Harvest and eat together — wash and taste the peas, cook the potatoes — closing the loop from soil to snack.
Talk through and record the changes — first shoots, flowers, fruit — and mark the seasons the patch moves through.
key_questions: What do you think our seeds need to grow?
How has the plant changed since last week?
What might we find if we dig down here?
When do you think these will be ready to eat?
How does it taste, now we've grown it ourselves?

impact.text: Children plant, harvest and help care for growing things as a real responsibility.
Children show care for plants with reminders — watering, gentle hands, patience.
Children observe change and growth over time and notice the seasons.
Children dig, rake, carry and pour, building whole-body strength and control.
Children ask real questions about how things grow and expect real answers.

enhancements: A pure digging pit — just soil and tools — for the youngest to dig, pour and find worms.
A growing diary with children's drawings and photos charting each plant week by week.
A harvest-to-kitchen link — the peas and potatoes go straight to the mud kitchen or a real cooking session.
A sunflower-height competition, measuring and comparing as they race skyward.
A seed-saving jar so this year's harvest sows next year's patch.

playing_exploring: Children dig, explore soil and handle seeds and worms with hands-on delight.
The patch invites open investigation of what's underground and how things grow.
active_learning: Children tend their plants patiently over weeks, sustaining care towards a distant reward.
Harvesting and eating their own food is a powerful, motivating payoff.
creating_thinking: Children predict what seeds need and what will happen, then test it over time.
They connect seed, plant, flower, fruit and food into a real understanding of growth.
